Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing up questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thornton, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Sarah Kline, Chief Medical Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: average reimbursement rates by payer category, capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, operating margin by segment, initiatives to improve operating margin, and same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year.

Let me begin with average reimbursement rates by payer category. In the hospitals and healthcare services space, payer mix and reimbursement dynamics are critical to our margin performance, particularly with ongoing CMS rulemaking, commercial payer negotiations, and the shift toward value-based care. For Q3, our net revenue per adjusted patient day came in at $2,450, up 4.2% year-over-year, primarily driven by favorable case mix index expansion to 1.68 from 1.62 last year, along with modest rate improvements. Breaking it down by payer category—Medicare, Medicaid, commercial/managed care, and other—we use blended average reimbursement per service or encounter, normalized to Medicare's IPPS DRG base rates for consistency.

Medicare, which makes up 42% of our payer mix, held steady at 102% of costs, or about $1,820 per adjusted patient day. This reflects the FY2024 IPPS final rule's 5.1% payment update, including a 3.8% market basket increase partially offset by a -0.2% productivity adjustment. We benefited from outlier payments, boosting this segment 2.1% year-over-year, especially in high-acuity ortho and cardio cases at our flagship facilities in Texas and Florida. Our Southeast markets outperformed the national average by 150 basis points due to higher wage index factors in urban areas like Miami-Dade with a 1.15 index. For FY2025, we're enhancing HCC risk adjustment coding through our Epic EHR implementation, lifting RAF scores by 8% in our Medicare Advantage subset, now 22% of total Medicare volume. We're also advancing bundled payments under BPCI Advanced, achieving 4% savings on lower extremity joint replacements and preserving shared savings upside.

Medicaid, 18% of our mix, remains challenging at 78% of costs or $1,420 per adjusted patient day, flat year-over-year despite state-directed payment programs. In California, Medi-Cal rates rose 3% after Prop 35 funding, but volumes dropped 5% in our LA basin hospitals due to post-pandemic redeterminations. In Texas, our managed care contracts with Superior HealthPlan provided a 6% uplift through value-based adders for sepsis management, hitting 92% HEDIS compliance. Nationally, it contributed just 1.2% to revenue growth, but telehealth expansions under state waivers have stabilized ED utilization. We anticipate 2-3% growth in 2025 as redeterminations stabilize, while advocating for parity with Medicare via state hospital associations.

Commercial/managed care, 35% of our mix, was the standout at 142% of Medicare rates or $3,280 per adjusted patient day, up 5.8% year-over-year from mid-year renegotiations with Blue Cross Blue Shield affiliates and UnitedHealthcare. We secured 4-6% unit rate increases on 65% of our commercial book, tied to acuity-based pricing using SOI and ROMI data. Aetna's narrow networks pressured Midwest margins by 200 basis points, but Cigna partnerships preserved premium rates for electives. PBM pressures from CVS Caremark on 340B drugs dipped ASP to 115% of WAC due to gross-to-net erosion, countered by our denial management AI, reducing appeals backlog by 35%. Northeast markets like NYC command 155% of Medicare, while rural Midwest lags at 130%.

Other payers, 5% of mix including self-pay and VA/Tricare, reached $1,950 per adjusted patient day, up 7% via patient financial services tech like Waystar, improving upfront collections to 45%. VA and Tricare stayed at 110% of Medicare with growth from Community Care Network contracts.

Overall, blended reimbursements grew 4.5% year-over-year, outpacing 3.1% case mix-adjusted cost inflation for 110 basis points of margin expansion. Site-neutral policies like CMS OPPS cuts are accelerating our ambulatory strategy, with 28% outpatient volume via JV ASCs. Our NLP-powered CDI program with 3M 360 Encompass captured $45 million in CMI lift year-to-date. Sunbelt expansion—TX, FL, AZ now 55% of beds—yields 8% higher blended ASPs versus legacy Midwest amid demographics and leverage. We see 4-5% growth in FY2025, assuming 3.5%+ IPPS update and strong commercial renewals, though MA denials—with 15,000 appeals at 75% overturn—and Medicaid volatility are risks. Our payer team targets 10% of book for risk-sharing pilots like HCA's.

Next, capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion. These remain central to driving organic growth, better outcomes, and market share in the $1.2 trillion U.S. healthcare services market. For full-year 2024, we deployed $2.15 billion in CapEx, up 12% from $1.92 billion in 2023, within our $2.1 to $2.2 billion guide. This is about 4.2% of our trailing 12-month revenue of $51.3 billion, above peers like HCA at 4% and UHS at 3.5%, reflecting our aggressive stance amid Baby Boomer-driven 15-20% Medicare inpatient day growth through 2030 per CMS.

Modernization took 62% or $1.33 billion, upgrading infrastructure for value-based care and post-COVID demands. We invested $450 million in advanced surgical suites and robotics, deploying 45 da Vinci Xi systems across 32 hospitals in Florida and Texas, lifting OR utilization to 78% and minimally invasive procedures 14% year-over-year at 20-30% higher MS-DRG reimbursements. $380 million went to EHR optimization, migrating 60% to Oracle Health Millennium with AI analytics, cutting clinician documentation 22% per KLAS benchmarks for bundled ortho/cardio success. $250 million covered diagnostic imaging like 120 Siemens Magnetom Avanto MRIs and Trane HVAC retrofits, cutting Midwest energy costs 18% amid 12% national rises and boosting radiology throughput 15%. Southeast got 42% of spend, including $120 million for Florida resiliency post-Hurricane Ian.

Expansion used 38% or $820 million for ambulatory and de novo builds capturing outpatient margins of 25-30% vs. inpatient 15-20%. $500 million built 12 new ASCs and micro-hospitals adding 450 bed equivalents and 28 ORs; our $180 million 200-bed freestanding ER/hospital in Dallas-Fort Worth opened Q3 at 85% utilization with 40% commercial mix via Blue Cross Texas. $320 million added 1,200 net beds in Sunbelt like Arizona/Nevada, addressing 12% bed shortages per AHA, under our hub-and-spoke model like HCA's for EBITDA gains.

CapEx drives 15-18% EPS CAGR through 2026 with 3-4 year paybacks on modernization and 4-5 on expansions. For 2025, guide $2.3-2.5 billion, 55% modernization including AI/telehealth like Nuance Dragon, 45% expansion with five USPI ASC JVs. This mitigates IPPS risks and builds moats vs. disruptors.

Turning to the impact of acuity mix changes on revenue. Acuity mix—the blend of high vs. low-acuity cases—is key to revenue via CMI weighting MS-DRGs and commercial contracts. In Q3, system-wide CMI rose 3.2% to 1.92, third straight quarter up from 1.85 in Q2, adding $128 million or 2.1 points to revenue per adjusted admission growth of 4.8%. At our 85-hospital, 4,200-bed scale across 18 states, each 1% CMI lift adds $45 million. High-acuity MS-DRGs 3.0+ like cardiac, neuro, sepsis now 42% of mix from 38%, boosting revenue per case 5.6% to $17,200 beyond 2.9% volume.

Drivers include post-COVID advanced disease presentations—oncology CMI up 4.1%—Boomer demographics for 12% vascular/pulmonary growth, 6% commercial uptick at 15% above Medicare, and managed observation at 18% ED via reviews. Sunbelt (55% beds) CMI up 4.5% to 1.98; Florida ortho/spine +22%, Texas neuro/stroke +18% via telestroke. Northeast +1.8% offset by outpatient JVs.

Operations: Epic MyChart at 85% improved documentation 14%, AI coding cut DRG downgrades to 4.5%; sepsis pathways +25% MS-DRG 870-872, Edwards TAVR +35% at $45k/case; Optum360 coding +1.2% CMI. $250M capex for hybrid ORs, Tempus oncology, $180M AZ acquisition for 2.1+ CMI. Amid 28% risk revenue, acuity buffers bundles/ACOs.

Q4 CMI 1.93-1.96 with flu/electives; FY25 IPPS risks modeled, target 45% high-acuity by 2026.

On operating margin by segment. Our consolidated adjusted operating margin hit 14.2%, up 210 bps from 12.1%, sixth straight quarter ahead of HCA/Tenet at 12-13%.

Acute Care Hospitals (62% revenue): $1.2B up 5%, margins 11.8% +180 bps. Admissions +3%, CMI 1.85 +2%; Medicare +4% IPPS $25M; labor +2.5% via AI scheduling, Vizient GPO 8% supplies. Sunbelt 13.5%, Northeast 9.2% offset by value-based.

ASCs (18%): $420M +12%, 32.4% +150 bps. Volumes +15% Optum JVs; site-neutral 40-50% below HOPD, da Vinci 70% +20% throughput, denials <2%. Sunbelt 35%, Midwest 28%.

Behavioral Health (12%): $285M +8%, 18.5% >UHS 15%. Days +6% opioid demand, commercial 55%; telehealth 30% visits -12% bad debt. Southeast 20.2%, PNW 16.8%; $50M crisis units to 22%.

Physician Services (8%): $185M +10%, 16.2% +170 bps. 1,200 FTEs +7%, wRVUs 4,800 +5% ScribeMD; TX/FL 18%.

Q4 15% with $100M Epic savings; ASC/behavior tuck-ins 20% capex, MSSP 15% below benchmarks, 35% value-based.

Now, initiatives to improve operating margin. We hit 6.8% consolidated, +140 bps from 5.4%, TTM 6.2% toward 8-10% by 2026, via labor, supply, RCM, throughput amid labor/supply inflation, payer shifts, value-based transition.

Labor (55% OpEx): agency to 6% from 18%, float pools/retention/Aya; Southeast -45% agency, AI LeanTaaS -22% OT +30 bps. Supply (22%): Vizient 7.2% cut, PPI std -15% $28M; Midwest hub -12% logistics/Medtronic.

RCM: denials 7.8% from 11.5%, AR 42 vs 48 peer; Epic/3M $45M underpayments, commercial $14,200 +4.1%, West prior auth +2.5 pts.

Throughput: LOS 4.6 from 4.9, CMI 1.68; da Vinci 75% OR +15% high-acuity, ASCs 18% volume, telehealth +35% -25% no-shows, MSSP $12M ortho 12% margins.

FY2024 +100-150 bps despite IPPS; home/behavior adjacencies.

Finally, same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance. Q3 same-facility net patient revenue +4.8%, admissions +2.7% organic at 145 hospitals/28 states, Sunbelt heavy.

Q4: admissions 2.0-2.5%, inpatient flat-0.5% elective dip offset ED 3.5-4.0%; days 1.5-2.0%, ALOS 4.6; outpatient 5.0-6.0% ortho/GI/pain 6-7% da Vinci CMI +1.2. Revenue 4.5-5.0%, NRPAA 2.0-2.5% MA 3.7% IPPS/commercial; Sunbelt 3-3.5%, NE/MW 1-1.5% telehealth 12% ED.

FY2025: admissions 3.0-3.5%, inpatient 1.0-1.5% oncology; days 2.5-3.0%, outpatient 6.0-7.0% ASC 8-10%; revenue 5.5-6.0%, NRPAA 2.5-3.0% 2.8% IPPS +4% commercial.

Pillars: service lines behavior/musculo CMI +2.5; labor 52% rev <10% agency; tech Guardant/Tempus 15% oncology, ACO 2.5M lives $120M savings.

Risks MA cuts/seasonal, upside elective/supply.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Michael to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $12.8 billion, an increase of 5.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and successful revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $11.1 billion, representing 86.7% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.28 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Integrated Care Pathways program has shown promising results, with a 25% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, which now supports virtual consults and has boosted access by 35% while cutting no-shows.

Following that, Raj will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including centralized supply chain management and AI-powered workforce scheduling, which have resulted in $150 million in cost savings year-to-date, with agency utilization down to 6% and supply costs per case reduced by 7.2%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Lisa for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include GenAI clinical decision support and a blockchain-secured patient data exchange platform, which directly address rising chronic disease prevalence and care coordination in fragmented markets, projecting 10-15% efficiency gains.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: please press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of centralized supply chain management?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Absolutely. Our centralized supply chain initiative, deepened via Vizient GPO commitments, delivered a 7.2% reduction in supply costs per case mix-adjusted discharge. For high-volume orthopedic implants and cardiac stents, PPI standardization cut variability 15%, saving $28 million annualized. In the Midwest, a new distribution hub shaved logistics 12%, strengthening negotiations with Medtronic and Stryker. Overall, this contributed about 40 basis points to margin expansion this quarter, with more to come as we standardize further.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Great question, Mike. Telehealth is transforming access, now handling 30-35% of outpatient visits and 12% of ED encounters network-wide. It has reduced no-shows by 25% via Epic MyChart and lowered bad debt 12% with real-time verification. Revenue-wise, expect 15-20% growth from telehealth in 2025, particularly in behavioral health and chronic care, adding 50 basis points to overall growth while supporting value-based models under state waivers and payer contracts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Emily. We're allocating $380 million from CapEx to EHR AI modules like Oracle Health and Nuance Dragon, plus $150 million for da Vinci expansions and pilots with Tempus/Guardant for precision oncology and liquid biopsies. Partnerships include USPI for ASC JVs and Optum for directed volumes. These target 5-7% CMI lift and 10% procedure growth, addressing chronic diseases with 15% oncology upside and ACO savings scaling to $120 million.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ramirez with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Ramirez:
Given the reimbursement details, how are you positioning for FY2025 payer pressures?

Michael Thornton:
David, thanks. Our 4-5% reimbursement growth guide assumes CMS 3.5%+ IPPS and commercial 4-6% uplifts from renewals. We're countering MA denials with 75% appeal success on 15,000 cases and risk-sharing pilots on 10% of book. Regional leverage in Sunbelt—8% higher ASPs—and CDI AI capturing $45 million CMI lift position us well, with Medicaid stabilizing at 2-3% via advocacy.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
